findings.text: Request descriptor separates caller visible transport and message buffers from private control. Private control tracks owning task and credential, transaction identifier, congestion accounting flag, short history of prior security sequence numbers with valid count, scratch pages for privacy transforms with release hook, alternative linkage for slot versus receive ordering, two send queue nodes, encode and reply areas with lengths, progress counters for bytes moved in each direction, private soft interrupt receive area, timeout alarms plus current timeout, round trip measurement, retry tally, connection generation cookie, pin count, partial send offset, transmit timestamp and transmit tally, plus optional callback list membership and preallocation state when callback support is enabled.

Transport object carries reference count, operations table, numeric identity, timeout profile, peer address with length and protocol number, current load and window, maximum payload, four wait queues for binding sending in flight and backlog, free slot list with maximum minimum and total counts, bitmask state word, low port and port reuse flags, swap usage count and bind selector index.

Same transport continues with multipath linkage, bind and reestablish timeouts, transport security parameters, connection generation cookie, cleanup work with timer and idle and connect timing values, queue length, three spinlocks for transport data slot table and send receive queues, next transaction identifier with blocked sender pointer, transmit queue with length, callback transport with optional service and preallocation counters list and guarding lock, receive tree, statistics block for binds connects timings completions lookup misses slot peaks and utilizations, network namespace with tracker, server and address strings, optional debug directory, reclaim hook, class pointer, sysfs node and primary transport marker.

Transport behavior is delegated through a table covering buffer sizing, exclusive reservation and release, slot allocation and release, name binding and port assignment, connection establishment, source address and port queries, task buffer allocation and release, request preparation sending abort waiting timing and release, close destroy, connect timeout configuration, statistics printing, swap enable and disable, forced disconnect, and a callback family for setup payload limit slot count request release and teardown.

Transport security offers three policy choices for clear versus anonymous versus certificate authenticated protection. Parameters pair the chosen policy with key identifiers for certificate and private key material.

Creation descriptor supplies transport identity, network namespace, optional local and required remote addresses with length, server name, callback transport and switch, flag word, security parameters and connect timers. Class registry links entries holding identity, setup callback, owner, short name and network identifier list.

Multipath switch holds guarding spinlock, reference count, switch identity, totals for transports active transports and distinct destinations, queue length, transport list, namespace, iterator operations, sysfs node and reclaim hook. Iterator holds switch reference under read copy update, cursor transport and operations pointer. Iterator operations provide rewind and access to current and next transport.

When the feature is enabled the per task dispatch record holds a user selector pointer with trap range offset and length plus a flag indicating entry from dispatch. When disabled the record is an empty placeholder.
System core operations table offers suspend resume and shutdown callbacks taking opaque data. Registration node links the table with its data into a global list.

Framebuffer support describes a machine family enumeration with roughly three dozen model variants plus an unknown placeholder, a table entry carrying option name base stride dimensions and flags, and a display bundle combining firmware screen description with optional extended display data when firmware table support is enabled.
Slot table sizing fixes minimum 2, default 16, and absolute ceiling 65536, with the working maximum equal to that ceiling.

Congestion control shift is 8, scale is 256 and initial window equals scale. Maximum window scales the transport slot maximum by the same shift. A transport counts as congested when current load has reached its window. Security history holds 3 entries. Address formatting enumerates address port protocol hexadecimal address hexadecimal port network identifier plus a count sentinel.

Backchannel marker is the top bit. Transport identities reuse protocol numbers for datagram and stream, set the marker for callback variants over those carriers, and assign fresh small integers 256 through 258 for direct memory, its callback variant, local, and protected stream, with callback direct memory formed by combining the base value with the marker.
Transport state bit positions start with locked 0, connected 1, connecting 2, close wait 3, bound 4, binding 5 and closing 6.
Remaining state positions assign offline 7, removal 8, congestion 9, window wait 10, write space 11 and cookie send marker 12.

Kernel log control actions number close through console level as 0 through 8 in order. System information selection bits use single bit masks from 1 through 128 for tasks memory timers locks tracing console replay full backtrace and blocked tasks.

Backchannel preallocation uses value 1. Creation flags use bit 0 for unbounded slots and bit 1 for disabling idle timeout. Compression scratch allowance is 61440. Callback notify result size equals the status size. Legacy system call names alias to a common old call handler, covering wait process identity status signal and mask queries.

Transport data is guarded by three distinct spinlocks for general transport fields, slot table reservation, and send receive queue linkage, while callback preallocation has its own spinlock and multipath switch state has another. Statistics and state bits use atomic or bit operations rather than these locks.

Iterator access to the switch pointer relies on read copy update with reclamation through the switch reclaim hook, and cursor movement is mediated by the iterator operations rather than direct list manipulation.

Connection progresses from idle through connecting to connected with explicit clear on teardown, and binding progresses from unbound through binding to bound with ordered clearing. Closing offline and removal record teardown, while congestion window wait and write space mediate send throttling and cookie mode marks cookie based sending.
Sequence history insertion saturates its valid count at capacity, shifts older entries toward the tail to free the head, stores the newest value at the head, and always reports success.
Send vector and length are aliases for the head and length of the send buffer. Backchannel preallocation test reports the unit flag when callback support is present and reports false otherwise.

Swap control delegates directly to the transport operations table for enable with status result and for disable without result. Small state helpers set clear test and atomic test and set or clear individual connection and binding bits, with ordered clearing for transitional connecting and binding states.

Byte order support aliases narrow wide and word swap forms plus pointer and in place variants to architecture primitives, and provides array helpers that walk a caller supplied buffer applying the in place conversion to each element.

Core synchronization hooks are empty. When dispatch support is absent the trap query and clear helpers report false, configuration getters and setters fail, and work clearing is empty. When present the clear on dispatch helper clears the per task flag exactly once. Framebuffer helpers are inert no operation or negative results, with mode parsing reporting false and simple framebuffer creation failing.

Transports are created through class setup callbacks registered by identity with ownership and naming, and all input output lifecycle and callback behavior flows through the operations table so concrete carriers implement reservation sending timing and teardown.

Request and transport objects mix reference counting pinning and read copy update reclamation with multiple locks, so misuse of slot versus receive linkage, unsynchronized statistics, or teardown racing timer cleanup and callback preallocation can corrupt queues. Window arithmetic scales slot counts and must not overflow, and disabled feature builds silently change dispatch preallocation and framebuffer behavior to false or failure.
